title: Debating
examples: How do I structure my arguments when I disagree with someone?
What makes a rebuttal strong enough to change someone's mind?
Should I focus more on my points or on responding to the other side?

explain.say: Today we will learn how to join a debate effectively. We will look at the main sides of an argument.
The proposition team argues that a statement is true. They must present reasons why it should be accepted.
The opposition team argues the opposite of the proposition. They must show why the statement is flawed.
A rebuttal is when you directly answer a point made by the other side. You must show why their point is wrong.

items: You provide evidence to counter it

explain.say: Respect means listening carefully even when you disagree. You must address the point, not the person.

draw.text: Respect: Address the argument, not the person

explain.say: In daily life, when friends argue about the best movie, you can use these skills. You can argue a side and rebut their points.

items: Best Movie | Action film is best | Comedy film is best

faq.q: What is the difference between a rebuttal and a counter-argument?
faq.a: A counter-argument is presenting your own opposing idea. A rebuttal is specifically pointing out a flaw in the opponent's argument.
asks: How do I disprove what they said?

faq.q: Do I have to agree with the proposition or opposition?
faq.a: No, you must argue the side assigned to you for that debate. Your job is to convince the audience of your side's viewpoint.
asks: Can I change my mind during the debate?
Do I have to believe what I say?

faq.q: What is the most important part of being respectful?
faq.a: It means maintaining a calm and polite tone. You can disagree strongly while still being polite to your opponents.
asks: Can I interrupt if I think they are wrong?
Is it okay to raise my voice?

faq.q: How many points should I make in my initial speech?
faq.a: It is better to make three clear, well-supported points. This gives you structure and time to rebut later.
asks: Should I use as many points as possible?
Do I need an introduction and conclusion?

faq.q: If I don't know how to rebut, what should I do?
faq.a: You can acknowledge their point, and then pivot to showing why your side's evidence is stronger. Focus on comparing your evidence.
asks: What if I am caught off guard?
Can I just repeat my own points?

facts: A debate requires two opposing sides, the proposition and the opposition.
A rebuttal directly addresses and refutes a specific claim made by the other team.
Maintaining respect means attacking the argument, never the person.
Strong arguments use clear evidence to support their main points.

quiz.say: Team A argues that uniforms should be mandatory in schools. Team B argues against it. Team B making a point about the cost of uniforms is:
quiz.why: Team B is arguing against the statement, which is the role of the opposition.

wrong.1: The proposition team must argue in favor of the statement.
wrong.2: A rebuttal must directly answer a point, not just make a new one.
wrong.3: Respect is a manner, not a side of the argument.

quiz.say: The opposing team claims that technology harms focus. You respond by saying, 'While that is true, our evidence shows it also helps research.' This response is best described as:
quiz.why: You acknowledged their point but then used evidence to show why your side's argument is stronger.

wrong.0: You are not arguing the opposite side's side.
wrong.1: This is a strategic argument move, not just being polite.
wrong.3: This is a response to the other side, not your main point.

quiz.say: Which action best demonstrates respect during a heated debate?

options.show: Raising your voice to prove a point
options.say: Raising your voice to prove a point

quiz.why: This phrase validates their point before presenting your counter-argument, which is respectful.

wrong.0: Interrupting shows you value your own words over listening.
wrong.1: Ignoring it makes you look unprepared or dismissive.
wrong.2: Volume does not prove the truth of an argument.
